guide.title: Client setup
guide.subtitle: Copy the configuration for the coding tool you use and replace <YOUR_API_KEY> with your API key.
guide.keyHint: An API key is shown only once, when it is created; if you did not save it, create a new one under “API Keys” and come back. Every client uses the same URL and key.
guide.orShell: Or set environment variables in your shell
guide.protocolNote: Claude Code speaks the Anthropic protocol, Codex the Responses protocol, Gemini CLI the native Gemini protocol, everything else OpenAI Chat; the gateway converts by the account behind the model, and same-protocol routes have the least overhead.

claudeCode.s1: Put the env block below into ~/.claude/settings.json (create it if missing)
claudeCode.s3: Restart claude and run /status to confirm the Base URL points at the gateway

codex.s3: Start codex; the model can be any text model from the Models page

opencode.s2: Keep the key out of the file: the config uses {env:YZAPI_API_KEY}; export that variable in your shell
opencode.s3: Start opencode and pick the yzapi model with /models
opencode.s4: This is the OpenCode stable (V1) provider layout; OpenCode V2 uses providers / package / settings, so check the docs for the version you installed

geminiCli.s1: Export the two environment variables below
geminiCli.s2: Pick the model with -m or in ~/.gemini/settings.json
geminiCli.s3: This entry speaks the native Gemini protocol; the gateway can also route it to other providers’ models
geminiCli.s4: Gemini CLI only accepts an HTTPS base URL (localhost excepted), so point it at the gateway's HTTPS domain

cline.s1: Choose the API Provider in the extension settings
cline.s3: Save and send a message to verify
cline.anthropic: Or the Anthropic provider (recommended for Claude models)

sdk.s1: Any OpenAI / Anthropic compatible SDK can point straight at the gateway

custom.s1: Non-chat models (TypeSafe Jev, rerankers, classifiers) are not called on /v1/chat/completions but on their own path: POST /v1/<path> with that API's own JSON body, which must include a model field
custom.s2: The URL is the gateway root plus the path and the key is the same as for every other client; the gateway rewrites only model, injects the upstream key, forwards the rest verbatim and returns the reply unchanged
custom.s3: The custom models and paths you are allowed to use are listed below; replace <YOUR_API_KEY> with your key
custom.none: No custom endpoint model is configured, or your user group is not authorised for one; the examples below use TypeSafe Jev.

images.s1: An image model serves text-to-image, image-to-image (inpainting, multi-image composition) and variations: send JSON to /v1/images/generations for generation, and a multipart form with the image files to /v1/images/edits or /v1/images/variations
images.s2: The form must include a model field; other fields (prompt, n, size, quality, mask, ...) follow the upstream; the total upload size is bounded by the request body limit set by the admin
images.s3: The image models you are allowed to use are listed below; replace <YOUR_API_KEY> with your key and a.png / b.png / mask.png with your files
images.none: No image model is configured, or your user group is not authorised for one; the examples below use gpt-image-2.5.
